description: Default architecture, no weight assignment (random init, expected ~0% accuracy).
One attention head routes query at answer step j to prompt position SRC_POS[j] (position-one-hot Q/K, token one-hot V, copy block unembed), d=128, 1 layer, MLP zeroed.
Same copy circuit as copy-perm-d128-g4 but attention gain 1.0 (softer routing), to test how sharp the attention must be.
Same copy circuit with attention gain 0.5, to find the lower bound on routing sharpness.
Same copy circuit with attention gain 0.25, to find the lower bound on routing sharpness.
Same copy circuit with attention gain 0.1, to locate where routing sharpness breaks the copy.
Compact width: same copy circuit with d_model=79 (token 0..27, position 28..50, copy 51..78), gain 4.
Compact d_model=79 copy circuit at gain 0.25: checks whether the routing threshold moves with width.
Binary token codes: each token is a 5-bit +/-1 code (d 28->5 for tokens, d_model=33), copy block 5 bits, head = dot with codes.
Bits5 circuit with the attention-input LayerNorm removed (ln1 = identity); one-hot query then needs gain 40 to keep routing sharp.
Bits5 circuit with every LayerNorm removed (ln1, ln2, final_ln = identity): the network is linear except for softmax and ReLU.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at attention gain 4: tests whether the no-LN routing is still sharp enough at a small gain.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at attention gain 15: locating the no-LN routing threshold between gain 4 and 40.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at attention gain 100: checks that the no-LN routing stays correct at very sharp gains.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at gain 100 with d_ff=0 (MLP removed entirely): does the copy need the MLP at all?
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit with a second (all-zero, inert) block: checks that extra untouched layers do not change the copy.
Sanity check: same circuit with SRC_POS = identity (copy the prompt unchanged); should fail, since the answer is not the prompt.
Same circuit, but the separator answer positions copy from prompt position 7 instead of 3 (both are '_'): should still be 100%.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 1: lower end of the no-LN gain sweep.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 8: between the failing gain-4 and the 80% gain-15 runs.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 25: pins down the no-LN threshold between gain 15 and 40.
Failure test: token codes are 0/1 bits instead of +/-1. Dot product with 0/1 codes is not unique-max, so this should fail.
Undersized code: only 4 +/-1 bits (16 codes for 28 tokens). Tokens 16+ alias, and the '_' separator (26) aliases to 'k' (10), so the copy always fails. Shows 5 bits are the minimum.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 20: refining the no-LN threshold between gain 15 and 25.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 12: lower edge of the no-LN threshold (gain 8 fails, 15 gives 80%).
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 16: just above the gain-15 80% run, checking where the threshold saturates.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 30: checks the upper end of the no-LN gain range that works.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit with attention gain 0: uniform attention over the prefix, so the copy has no positional routing. Should fail.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at attention gain 60: an even sharper router, to confirm high gains do not break the copy.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit at attention gain 200: extreme router sharpness, to confirm there is no upper limit on the gain.
Same no-LN bits5 circuit padded to d_model=64 (31 unused zero dims): checks that the circuit does not depend on the width being minimal.
Failure test: copy block placed on top of the token-code dims (COPY_OFF=0). Own token then contaminates the read-out, so this should fail.

Copy block placed on top of position-one-hot dims 5..9 (COPY_OFF=5). Still 100%: query positions 11..21 have no one-hot bit in those dims, so the write does not collide. Expected a failure; it does not.
Bits5 circuit with LayerNorm restored (ln1 and final_ln) at attention gain 0.5: how sharp must routing be when LN is present?
Bits5 circuit with LayerNorm restored (ln1 and final_ln) at attention gain 2.
Bits5 circuit with LayerNorm restored (ln1 and final_ln) at attention gain 8.
Bits5 circuit with LayerNorm restored (ln1 and final_ln) at attention gain 1.
Bits5 circuit with LayerNorm restored (ln1 and final_ln) at attention gain 16.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 35: inside the 25..60 range where the no-LN circuit is fully correct.
No-LayerNorm bits5 circuit (d_ff=0) at attention gain 50: final point of the no-LN gain sweep, inside the fully-correct range.
